reason: This leg is three days old and was built for precisely the macro outcome that has since been confirmed, so trading it now would be paying friction to re-express a view that is already on. The 2026-09-16 FOMC raised the target range to 3.75-4.00% with the statement still calling inflation elevated and the labour market steady - a genuine tightening into an inflationary economy, not the cutting cycle the high-multiple market is priced for (SPY 25.1x at 761.69, near its 779 high, led by AI weights). In that regime the book's two engines are the right ones and neither has been invalidated. (1) Hard-asset energy: Brent is testing $100, XLE is +47.4% over twelve months yet still only 16.9x, and my names are priced well below even that - CVX 13.1x forward, COP 13.2x forward with a strong Q2 at $3.23/sh and $1.7bn of disposals done, XOM flat on the leg. Chevron's own CEO is publicly flagging depleted crude buffers. The commodity has re-rated faster than the equities, so the discount I bought is still there; selling it because the underlying finally moved is exactly the deep-value error of harvesting a thesis one quarter before it pays. (2) The cheapest defensives are cheaper than when I bought them: CVS is down 3.1% on the leg on nothing - the only news is Aetna oncology prior-auth changes and vaccine expansion - while sitting at 10.9x forward against a 27-analyst Strong Buy and a $116 consensus, PFE is 10.0x forward yielding 6.22% (a ~220bp spread over the 4% cash alternative that just got harder for the market to ignore), BMY is 9.8x forward with a fresh CELMoD approval and Piper Sandler moving to $82. Marking a 3% drawdown in CVS as a reason to cut would be selling the widest gap in the book. The short XLP funding leg is the cleanest expression of the hike: 21.4x and a 2.65% yield for no real growth, with the front end at 4% and rising, and it has already contributed +0.64%. Every one of the eight legs is inside its stop, the worst is -3.1%, and the catalysts that close these gaps - CVS 10/28, BMY 10/29, CVX 10/30, PFE 11/3 - all sit ahead of the next few marks, not behind. Against that, a full replacement costs 2bps a side plus SEC/TAF on the sells across an 86%-gross book to buy essentially the same exposure, and would reset every stop to a worse basis. The 14% cash is deliberate: it earns 4% and is my optionality if the Saudi barrels that knocked 1% off crude turn into a real supply response and hand me energy cheaper. Note on process: this session's WebSearch budget was exhausted before my first query, so all research above was done with direct WebFetch against the Federal Reserve statement and per-name quote and news pages, which is why this reason cites hard valuation and price data rather than a broad sentiment sweep.
